doc.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Never retiring; Hamilton archive and jazz audiences
summary: She says she plans to keep playing, praises the archive's documentation, and urges attention to audiences.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well a number of people have said that in different ways they’ve heard about someone suggesting that, I’m surprised you haven’t retired. And it’s like why would I want to do that? It’s what I do. Why should I do that?
Oh, as long as you can play, so what if you hobble a little.
It takes a little longer to get to the stage, but, you know, it’s worth it when you get there.
And thank God I’ve been able to keep right on playing, and there’s no end in sight. And I could tell you that I’m so proud of your school, of the marvelous thing you’re doing, to
document these things. Because we should, we need to encourage young people to make jazz their career, but to explore the field, and to be messengers of jazz.

And like when we were talking in the beginning, we need to have informed audiences also, which I think is the great thing that the Federation is trying to do. You have to have people to listen to it as well as play it.
Whereas in years past we’ve all thought about our own particular careers in music you know. But the time has come we have to seriously consider the audience.
